$comment: Applied output of the cultural-calendar agent for May 2026 — Kerala-leaning South Indian veg restaurant. Hero hook = Akshaya Tritiya (May 19) which is the most relevant May festival for the Kerala/Tamil/Telugu/North Indian diaspora that drives this restaurant's traffic. Mother's Day is a secondary US-calendar hook. AAPI Heritage Month is small angle. Indian wedding season runs through May for catering inquiries.
seasonal_notes: Late spring in Loudoun — Indian wedding season peaks (May–June), school is winding down (LCPS last day mid-June 2026), and Akshaya Tritiya is the spring's commercial concentrator for South Asian businesses. Weather warm enough for outdoor pickup; not yet the summer mango-season window.

hooks.name: Akshaya Tritiya
hooks.significance: Auspicious day for new beginnings, gold purchases, business starts. In Kerala specifically, families often eat a special sadya or Kerala-traditional meal. Strong commercial-intensity day — second only to Onam for a Kerala-leaning restaurant.

restaurant: Akshaya Tritiya sadya — full banana-leaf feast, 18 items, $24/plate, two seatings
Pre-book the sadya 1 week ahead — limit 30 plates per seating
Kerala-style payasam (boli, palada pradhaman, ada pradhaman) as the closer; one per seating, named by day

do_not_say: auspicious feast for an auspicious day
embrace the spirit of Akshaya Tritiya

hooks.name: Mother's Day
hooks.significance: US-calendar hook; South Indian families often do a Sunday lunch out instead of brunch. Secondary to Akshaya Tritiya for this client — don't blow the email on Mother's Day when the bigger spend is Akshaya Tritiya nine days later.

restaurant: Sunday lunch with amma — regular menu, no upcharge, no pre-fixe gimmick
Filter coffee + parippuvada combo for the table; reminds the elders of home
Walk-ins all day; no reservation required (run the regular Sunday flow)

do_not_say: celebrate the woman who does everything

hooks.name: AAPI Heritage Month
hooks.significance: Cultural recognition month; Aditi's is AAPI-owned, the operator can lean into it lightly but the diaspora audience won't react to a 'celebrating AAPI Heritage Month' framing — they want the food. Use it as a small post or a thank-you nod, not a campaign pillar.

restaurant: Light acknowledgement post: 'small Kerala kitchen, AAPI Heritage Month' + one dish photo
Skip if it would replace an Akshaya Tritiya slot

hooks.name: Buddha Purnima
hooks.significance: Vesak / Buddha Purnima. Relevant to a small subset of the customer base. Light vegetarian-only angle (already vegetarian — no menu change). Skip if calendar is already full.

restaurant: Quiet note in a Sunday post — 'fully vegetarian, every day' — nothing more

hooks.name: Indian wedding season
hooks.significance: May–June is peak North Indian + South Indian wedding season in the Loudoun diaspora. Catering inquiries spike — small mehndi/sangeet snack packs, weekday-lunch sadya orders, sweets boxes. Aditi's isn't a full caterer in v1 but should signal availability for 30–60 person small orders.

restaurant: Mehndi/sangeet snack tray — parippuvada + bonda + chutney boxes, 24h notice, 30+ people
Tray pickup, not delivery — the kitchen is one tava, not a catering operation
Sadya catering: $22/head for 30+, banana leaf included, two days' notice

do_not_say: wedding food fit for a queen
we cater to all your needs
